title: Schema Variables (Textable, Record)
description: Schema Variables object with key-value pairs
documentation:
## Purpose

Schema Variables carry a JSON object of key-value pairs that are injected into a schema before validation or generation. They allow schemas to be templated and reused across different contexts by varying only the variable bindings.

## When to use

Use this media type when a node consumes a parameterized schema and needs the variable bindings resolved at runtime. It is similar in structure to [Substitutions](https://capdag.com/browse/media:substitutions;textable;record) but scoped specifically to schema processing.

## Notes

Variable names should match the placeholder tokens defined in the schema. Unresolved variables may cause validation failures, so ensure all required keys are present before passing this value downstream.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.
